A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
early, long-term antiretrovial therapy of perinatal HIV infection is associated with a latent reservoir dominated by defective, non-induced provirus.
early, long-term antiretrovirus therapy of perinatal HIV-1 infection results in marked diminution of the replication competent HIV-1 reservoir.
early and effective treatment of HIV infection can reduce the reservoir of replication competent virus to a level that is undetectable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the latent reservoir of HIV is very difficult to measure and is not well understood.
early initiation of ART and long-term virolgoic suppression of perinatal HIV infection results in a paucity of intact, inducible proviruses.
early initiation of ART and long-term suppression can reduce the size of the HIV reservoir.
